module purpose: neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu is a single-precision floating-point co-processor: it decodes the instruction fields on ctrl_i, captures and classifies rs1_i and rs2_i when ctrl_i.alu_cp_fpu starts an operation, runs classify, compare, min/max, sign injection, integer/float conversion, multiply and add/subtract (with the neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu_normalizer and neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu_f2i sub-entities), registers the result on res_o with a valid_o strobe and per-operation exception flags, and holds the frm and fflags CSRs written through csr_we_i, csr_addr_i and csr_wdata_i and read on csr_rdata_o.

use-case flows.value: dynamic rounding mode (csr_frm) and accrued exception flags (csr_fflags) written from csr_wdata_i when csr_we_i is set and csr_addr_i selects the register
stored fflags and frm returned on csr_rdata_o as selected by csr_addr_i

decoded FPU operation accepted in S_IDLE when ctrl_i.alu_cp_fpu and cmd.valid are set: function code, cmp_i, applied rounding mode, operands and operand classes captured, start pulse raised and one function unit started
operand preparation: subnormal mantissas forced to zero and each operand classified into ten class bits
classify, compare, min/max and sign-injection results and flags computed from the captured operands, their classes and cmp_ff
conversions: float-to-integer in neorv32_cpu_cp_fpu_f2i (rounded by rmode_i) and the integer-to-float pre-stage in convert_i2f
multiply and add/subtract: mantissa product or aligned sum, exponent, sign, result class and flags handed to the normalizer, which normalizes, rounds by rmode_i and finalizes the packed result
sequencing: the engine stays in S_BUSY until a unit reports done or ctrl_i.cpu_trap is set; latency registers and the sub-unit state machines time each unit and abort on ctrl_i.cpu_trap
result and per-operation exception flags registered on res_o and fflags for one cycle when ctrl_engine.valid is set, valid_o strobe, flags accumulated into csr_fflags
rstn_i low clears frm and fflags, the engine state, captured operands, unit registers, res_o, fflags and the sub-unit state machines
